messages:
jordy: Quick perf dump from a small sweep: compared aggressive prefill (fill-ahead) vs on-decode cache population on g5.8x nodes. Observed latency vs token-cost tradeoffs + a few OOMs under spike traffic. TL;DR: prefill reduces token CPU by ~22% but increases p50 by ~10-15% and exposes fragmentation/OOMs at high concurrency.

jordy: Raw numbers (median across 10 runs):
jordy: - baseline (on-decode): p50=42ms p95=180ms tokens/sec=118 cost/token=1.00
jordy: - prefill-heavy (reserve 40% workspace): p50=48ms p95=260ms tokens/sec=145 cost/token=0.78 (but OOMs in 3/10 runs at concurrency=120)

jordy: - hybrid (soft per-request cap + lazy prefill): p50=44ms p95=200ms tokens/sec=135 cost/token=0.85 OOMs=0/10

emily: can you paste the allocator / slab stats? is this obvious slab fragmentation or just overall footprint?

jordy: pasted epoch-level allocator snaps: free_slab_frag=1.9GB -> 6.4GB after prefill runs; internal external fragmentation ratio jumps ~3x. Looks like many mid-sized allocations from KV prefill cause small-slab scatter.

jordy: ```
# experiment flags used
--kv_prefill_pct=0.4
--per_request_cap_mb=24
--allocator_compact_pass=false
--continuous_batching=on
```

jordy: Also saw kernel selection differences: with larger workspace reservation we hit a different matmul kernel that uses more temporary buffers during kv prefill which amplifies memory pressure.

santosh: that kernel shift is huge. we should add a telemetry tag for "kernel_variant" when prefill_enabled so we can correlate memory peaks with kernel choice.

emily: agree. Also think about: small per-request soft caps (e.g., 8MB) but allow aggregate prefetch reservation across host-level pool. That keeps latency low while letting prefill amortize.

perflab: perflab: uploaded profile: https://perf.internal/runs/1778906543 (flame, alloc timeline, kernel map). Added an annotation where workspace bump correlates with bulk kernel switch at t=00:02:14.

jordy: tried a quick mitigation: enabled slab compaction pass every 30s and introduced a per-request soft cap of 16MB + global kv_reserve=20%. Results: no OOMs, p50 hit +4ms, cost/token +6% vs aggressive prefill, but stable at scale.

emily: can you share the exact compact command and where we hook it? we need guardrails for production — compaction can't block hot decode threads.

jordy: compaction is background async GC on idle workspaces: `allocator.compact(passive=true, budget_ms=10)` scheduled on low-load heartbeats. Hook is runtime/allocator/idle_detector.

santosh: two follow-ups: 1) add kernel_variant telemetry, 2) try a decode-first prefill hybrid where we prefill only prefixes above 256 tokens or if expected seq_len > X. That way short requests don't pay prefill cost.

emily: also propose a fragmentation test harness: create synthetic workload with many medium-length sequences (50-300 tokens) interleaved with large ones, measure free_slab_frag and compaction effectiveness. If fragmentation correlates strongly with average seq_len distribution, we can tune slab bucket sizes.

jordy: Action items agreed:
- jordy: add kernel_variant tag + correlate in perf dashboard (ETA next day)
- santosh: implement decode-first hybrid policy gate with config flags `kv.prefill_threshold_tokens` and `kv.prefill_on_long_seq_only` (ETA 2d)
- emily: spin up fragmentation harness and run sweep for slab bucket sizes (ETA 3d)
- infra-bot: schedule a canary deployment window to test slab_compact_interval change on a small fleet at 2am PST

infra-bot: infra-bot: scheduled canary: 2026-03-20 02:00 PST, target group: runtime-canary-4, change: enable allocator passive compaction, soft per-request cap=16MB for 48h.

santosh: one more note — we saw that continuous batching heuristics interact with prefill: longer batching windows make prefill more beneficial but pushes latency tails. we'll need to expose batching window per route as a knob.

emily: +1. Also add a safety: if allocator reports >80% fragmentation for 60s, temporarily disable aggressive prefill and fall back to decode-only for that worker.

jordy: good call. I'll prototype the watchdog and a small dashboard alarm. thanks all — will post updated numbers after canary. :thumbsup:
